how: A starter had already worked alone on the proposed emblem before inviting the room to join.
The starter invites members to finish the mark, and another participant later reports seeking support by tweet.
The emblem begins as one member's proposal rather than a demonstrated collective design decision.
Members report a partly visible emblem, solo progress despite a glitch, and a later contribution of pixels.
A landmark description and linked target orient helpers without demonstrating a collectively agreed pixel template.
One participant assents to the proposal and another answers the solo-work update with a bare offer of help.
An instruction asks placers to spare neighboring art while permitting some overlap.
The starter reports granting limited overlap after a polite request, without preserving the negotiation or identifying a counterpart room.
Participants announce success and credit everyone, while other viewers congratulate the group without claiming construction labor.
The final-product claim and account of a simpler design becoming more complex minimally record the work's fate.
A glitch and partial progress do not establish watching, repair, or defense against erosion.
The glitch report does not trace who changed the work or assign responsibility.
An instruction to spare neighboring art provides no evidence of a preceding attack.
Reporting a glitch and visible progress does not establish erasure followed by relocation.
The post-close wish to keep the image unchanged names no successor canvas, reuse, or lasting organization.
The progress report identifies a glitch but does not establish scripts, bots, or spare accounts.
A tweet seeking support identifies neither a recipient room nor interroom help or reciprocity.
Outreach by tweet does not establish coalition membership or joint organization between rooms.
Collective success is celebrated without a named rival or a contest carried into talk.
Permission for limited neighboring overlap does not establish guests living under a host room's rule.
The call and contribution report establish canvas activity without showing host rules, redirection, or a boundary dispute.
Reported permission to overlap contains no challenge to who may commit the room to an agreement.
Praising complexity and wishing the image preserved do not establish a dispute over cleanup or which historical version to retain.
The emblem proposal does not establish host parody or April Fools keying.
Working alone does not itself express a judgment that the room lacks enough hands to make or hold its work.
The game-emblem proposal identifies no quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
Selecting a game emblem alone does not establish organizing through inherited quarrels, ideology, or color allegiance.
A personal start, voluntary help, and later pixel reports do not establish the absence of decided order elsewhere.
A proposal without a named rival cannot test whether a prior tie selected a target for attack.
The reported polite request identifies no person acting as an envoy between rooms.
The starter explicitly connects prior solo work to telling the room and asking others to make the emblem together.
A proposal receives bare assent, supporting the observable answer pattern without establishing why joining is preferred over declining.
The call precedes another participant's pixel report, but that participant does not say the call caused the contribution.
Build reports do not show whether upkeep followed or what prompted it.
The reported overlap request is not linked to an observed period of upkeep against erosion.
The starter attributes restraint to a polite request, but neither an independently observed settled border nor later compliance is preserved.
A glitch report supplies no upkeep-to-automation sequence or mechanism.
Build reports precede collective celebration, but the record does not establish that a completion report prompted the celebration.
Celebration and retrospective reporting share passages, leaving their proposed causal ordering unresolved.
A wish to preserve the result supplies no demonstrated transition from recording toward lasting reuse.
A solo-work report establishes neither a judgment of inadequate strength nor a resulting move.
The proposal and linked reference do not show a design argument being settled by a template.
The tweet report identifies no upkeep strain, recipient room, or help returned from another room.
Reported overlap permission is not connected to an exchange of help.
The build call does not show members turning their hands toward an attack.
Restraint is attributed to a polite request without a preserved preceding attack call.
The accommodation report does not establish that an attack prompted border talk.
Collective credit supplies neither an attack nor a subsequent contest with a named rival.
Seeking support by tweet establishes neither upkeep under attack nor resulting coalition membership.
The call and later contribution supply no observed flood or resulting host intervention.
The overlap accommodation supplies no subsequent challenge to who speaks for the room.
A report of working alone receives a direct offer of help, adding a progress-report route into bare joining.

statement: recognizing an existing community through its canvas mark
how: Seeing the finished mark reveals an existing community to one viewer and recalls past participation to another without establishing recruitment or a return to play.
